newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldovan 1996 grain harvest to fall to 1.74 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan 1996 grain harvest to fall to 1.74 mln T.

text.p: Moldova's 1996 grain harvest, including maize, will fall to 1.74 million tonnes from 2.39 million last year but Moldova will have enough to meet its needs, Agriculture Minister Vitalie Gorincioi said on Wednesday.

"Following a severe drought in the summer and torrential rains in September, the total grain harvest will fall this year to just 60 percent of what the government targeted initially," Gorincioi told a special parliament hearing on agriculture.

He said farmers had so far gathered 850,000 tonnes of early crops, including wheat, peas and barley, from over 430,000 hectares. He said that 890,000 tonnes of maize were being harvested from 248,000 hectares.

"In general, the republic will have enough grain until the next harvest," he said, adding that the state had so far bought over 150,000 tonnes of bread-making grain out of the 240,000 tonnes it needed from local producers.
"But the problem of stable grain supplies is still acute, so the government has issued an order to purchase 94,000 tonnes of maize for state reserves," Gorincioi said.
Some deputies criticised the agriculture ministry for the slow rate of winter crops sowing.
"Over 100,000 hectares out of 430,000 have not been yet sown. Next year's harvest may turn out to be no better, if the sowing is not completed within a few days," one parliamentarian said.

Gorincioi said agriculture, which accounts for over 60 percent of Moldova's gross domestic product, had fallen victim to the sector's debts of 2.3 billion lei to the government, energy suppliers and the social fund.
